note: PredicateStatus::as_str() writes 'partially_applied' into payload_json's status key (via json_set before, read-modify-write now), but the payload's serde round-trip expects camelCase 'partiallyApplied' — after update_predicate_status(PartiallyApplied), list_operations silently drops the row (serde_json::from_str fails and the op is skipped). Latent since Phase C; preserved bug-for-bug by the ADR-036 port (see plan_repo.rs update_predicate_status comment + pinning test).

sample_operations() reads cleanup_plan_operations.sample_ids_json, but save()/append_operations() never write that column (sample ids only live inside payload_json) — the method returns empty for every plan persisted through the repo. Pinned as current behavior by sample_operations_reads_column_save_never_populates; fixing means writing PlannedOperationPredicate.sample_email_ids into the column at insert (and deciding backfill).

CleanupPlanRepository::load() passes u32::MAX to list_operations, whose limit clamp(1,1000) silently truncates plans with >1000 operations — a >1000-row plan loads (and can be applied/reported) incomplete. Pre-existing (clamp identical at phase-1 marker 05036c9, plan_repo.rs:335); preserved by the SeaORM port.

OpsFilter.action compares the caller's token (e.g. "archive") against cleanup_plan_operations.action, which stores the JSON-serialized PlanAction (e.g. {"type":"archive"}) — the action filter can never match. Pre-existing; the old code's comment even claimed the column stores "the discriminant string", which insert never did.

update_operation_status sets the applied_at COLUMN but list_operations builds rows from payload_json only, whose appliedAt key is never synced — an applied operation reads back with applied_at=None. Pre-existing (old json_set synced only $.status); pinned by update_operation_status_syncs_payload_status_only.

cancel/list_operations/sample_operations are scoped by plan UUID only (no user_id filter, unlike load/list_by_user) — knowledge of another user's plan id permits reading its operations or cancelling it. UUIDv7 ids are unguessable but this is a defense-in-depth gap in the single-user-today, multi-tenant-groundwork (ADR-031) design. Pre-existing API/trait shape.

Classes flagged across the still-hand-rolled legacy-enum files that phase 3 re-ports: unchecked `as i32` narrowing (email/checkpoint.rs:121, cleanup/audit.rs:257, email/offline_queue.rs:215 — entity types fix the class), select-then-update dequeue races (email/offline_queue.rs dequeue, content/jobs.rs claim — content/jobs is not yet wired per Cargo.toml note), and apply.rs discarding a terminal job-state persist failure after emitting Finished (orchestrator/apply.rs ~:293-323). Phase 3 must not blindly preserve these; each needs a decision at port time.

vectors/audit.rs and vectors/consent.rs read PostgreSQL TIMESTAMP (no tz) columns as NaiveDateTime + .and_utc() (hardened in the wip commits) but still WRITE DateTime<Utc> binds, which Postgres assignment-casts timestamptz->timestamp using the session TimeZone GUC — on a non-UTC session, stored values shift by the offset and get relabeled UTC on read. Live verification can't catch it (postgres:16-alpine defaults to UTC; cr-bugscan's empirical check confirmed insert works but only on UTC). Fix at phase 3's entity port: bind .naive_utc() on writes (or entity NaiveDateTime type), or resolve for good in the queued db-schema-modernization TIMESTAMPTZ normalization.

Two files the wip commits claimed converted still carry raw state.db.pool() call sites (pool() PANICS on a Postgres connection): api/rules.rs has 5 (lines ~184, 498, 608, 724, 776 — list_rules match_count fetch, rule test/run email fetches, run_rule match_count persistence incl. a to_rfc3339 String bound into TIMESTAMPTZ, suggestions GROUP BY) and api/ingestion.rs has ~13 inside the two partially-converted sync functions. ~206 .pool() sites remain repo-wide — phase 3's grep:absent .pool() DoD forces the sweep; phase 3 must NOT trust wip commit messages' 'converted X and call sites' claims as complete.

Phase 4's CI postgres job must export EMAILIBRIUM_TEST_PG_URL (not only EMAILIBRIUM_DATABASE_URL) — the phase-2 live-Postgres repo tests (plan_repo/job_repo postgres_* tests) skip-and-pass when that variable is unset, so without it the CI job would run the suite against Postgres but silently skip the dedicated Postgres round-trip assertions.

begin_apply's status gate (orchestrator/apply.rs ~:150) checks the CALLER'S loaded plan snapshot, not a persistent atomic transition — two concurrent POST /apply for the same Ready plan both pass the gate and spawn duplicate workers over the same rows (duplicate mailbox side effects; and under ADR-036's read-modify-write status sync, one writer's status update can additionally be lost). Pre-existing TOCTOU, surfaced by the phase-2 overturn round. Fix shape: an atomic Ready->Applying compare-and-swap (conditional update_many on status, rows_affected==1 or reject 409) before spawning workers; needs its own tests. Do not fold into phase 3's mechanical port without a decision.

rules/executor.rs AddLabel (:124) and RemoveLabel (:171) are select-then-update read-modify-writes on emails.labels with no transaction/guard — two rules mutating labels concurrently lose one write. Same hazard class as the offline_queue dequeue / content jobs claim races phases 7/8 own; ported bug-for-bug by the ADR-036 port. AddLabel's already-present early-out (:144) is load-bearing for idempotence and preserved.

email/oauth.rs get_access_token decodes encrypted_access_token as non-optional Vec<u8> against a NULLABLE column — a disconnected account (tokens cleared by disconnect_account) errors on decode instead of surfacing AccountNotFound/a clean error. Pre-existing shape, preserved bug-for-bug by the ADR-036 port and commented at the call site. Fix belongs with a deliberate behavior-change review (phase 8 class), not the port.

cleanup_audit_log's module doc and BOTH migration-025 headers claim deletion cascades from cleanup_plans (ON DELETE CASCADE) giving right-to-erasure for free — but neither dialect's migration 025 declares any FOREIGN KEY, so erasing a plan does NOT erase its audit rows. GDPR-relevant documentation-vs-reality gap. Fix is a schema change (belongs to the queued db-schema-modernization pipeline or its own decision), not this port.

vectors/remote_wipe.rs wipe_user_data deletes FROM search_interactions WHERE user_id = ? — but migration 001 (both dialects) defines search_interactions WITHOUT a user_id column, so on any migrated database the statement errors and wipe_user_data ALWAYS fails after deleting only vector_backups (partial wipe, GDPR-relevant). Only the module's hand-rolled test schema, which invents a user_id column, passes. Ported bug-for-bug via an Expr::cust("user_id") filter (commented at the site); the real fix — either add the column by migration or scope interactions differently — is a schema/behavior decision for phase 7/8 or db-schema-modernization.

wipe_audit_log (the ADR-017 GDPR remote-wipe audit trail) has no migration in either dialect and no entity — its only schema definition is the per-backend runtime DDL in vectors/remote_wipe.rs ensure_table(). Pre-existing (predates phase 3); the other two runtime DDL replays (007 user_learning_models, 009 ab_tests) mirror real migrations verbatim, this one has nothing to drift from. Fix = give it a numbered migration + entity; belongs to db-schema-modernization or its own decision.

backend/tests/api_integration.rs 'replicates' production SQL in test-local axum handlers because AppState/api::routes() live in the binary crate and are not lib-exported — after the phase-3 port the replicas (raw SQL strings) and production (SeaORM Conditions) have structurally diverged, so its account-scoping tests (e.g. test_list_emails_filter_by_account_id, the disconnect test) would survive deletion of the production filters: false coverage. Root fix = export AppState/routes() from the lib crate and drive the real handlers; that is an architectural change beyond the phase-3 bug-for-bug port. Same root cause leaves api/accounts.rs disconnect_account (two destructive account-scoped delete_many) with no direct DB test — its handler needs AppState. Deferred with this record per the phase-3 court (floor-scoping findings 1/2); candidates: optimization pass or phase 8.

api/ingestion.rs sync_emails_from_provider's two account-scoped sync_state queries (history_id read; delta-failure history_id clear) are unpinned — they sit behind a live provider call, so a pin needs a provider fake. mark_sync_idle (the third scoped query in the file) has its two-owner test. Recorded deferral per the phase-3 court (floor-scoping finding 4).

vectors/remote_wipe.rs execute_pending_wipes: when at least one due wipe succeeds, the retention pass removes EVERY due schedule entry — including ones whose wipe just FAILED — so a failed scheduled GDPR erasure is silently dropped and never retried (it only survives if every wipe in the batch failed). Pre-existing logic, byte-identical to the pre-port code (verified against 27f7533); in-memory schedule semantics, untouched by the ADR-036 port. Filed by the phase-3 court's security-scanner seat; fix (retain failed entries, or per-entry removal) is a behavior change for phase 7/8.

The phase-3 entity port changes emails.received_at's on-disk write shape on SQLite: pre-port production writes were RFC3339 String binds only (one shape on disk); post-port NaiveDateTime binds write the naive 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' shape. TEXT comparison means within one day naive rows sort BELOW same-day RFC3339 rows (' ' < 'T') — on a live upgrade, newly synced same-day mail lists under pre-upgrade mail until the day rolls over. Cross-day ordering is correct. Pinned by mixed_shape_rows_interleave_within_one_day (api/emails.rs); prose there and in the entity doc corrected by the phase-3 court. Retirement (TIMESTAMPTZ normalization + legacy-row backfill) belongs to the queued db-schema-modernization pipeline.

Constructor signatures still take Arc<Database>/Database and immediately convert (conn: db.sea_orm()) — ~20 services — and AppState carries both handles (db 21 uses vs orm 75). Deliberate phase-3 scoping: keeping ctor signatures stable kept the 83-file port reviewable; the enum is now confined to the composition root plus constructor currency. Retiring it from signatures (ctors take DatabaseConnection; AppState.db shrinks to connect/migrate use) is mechanical API churn for the cross-phase optimization pass. Also fold cleanup/repository/adapters.rs onto the cached-conn pattern its siblings use, and consider consolidating the triplicated count_star()/i32-narrowing helpers then.

Delivered in phase 4: .github/workflows/ci.yml's rust-test-postgres job exports EMAILIBRIUM_TEST_PG_URL alongside EMAILIBRIUM_DATABASE_URL; verified locally that all three postgres_* round-trip tests RUN (not skip) under it, and the job is green on PR #260.

Mutation seat charge M7 (survivor, partially remediated): replacing main.rs's `db.startup_backend_line()` with a re-parse of config.database_url survives the entire suite AND both smoke legs, because config and reality agree in both. The property the diagnostic exists to protect — that the line follows the CONNECTION, not the requested config — therefore has no executable check at any level; only prose forbids it. startup_backend_line() pins the exact string smoke greps for, which is a different (and weaker) guarantee. A real pin needs a boot-level test where the connected backend and the configured URL deliberately disagree.

Devils-advocate charge D8 (accepted deviation): `depends_on.postgres.required: false` is required for the no-profile project to validate at all, but it does weaken the profile-active case — a postgres that fails to start no longer holds the backend back; the stack goes red through backend's own healthcheck instead. Documented in docker-compose.yml at the point of use, but no workflow exercises a delayed or unhealthy PostgreSQL, so the degraded path is asserted only in prose. Phase 4's DoD phrase 'wired the same way it is today' holds for the service definition (byte-identical plus `profiles:`) but NOT for the dependency condition.

Devils-advocate charge D5 (residual after remediation): smoke's PostgreSQL leg now proves the app WROTE to PostgreSQL (successful rows in _sqlx_migrations) on top of the startup log line, but still exercises no application-data write/read through an endpoint, because the DB-backed endpoints are authenticated. A seeded user + one authenticated round trip would raise this from 'migrations ran' to 'the app can store and retrieve email data on PostgreSQL'.

Security-scanner charge S1 (accepted): rust-test-postgres publishes the service container as 5432:5432 with a known throwaway password. GitHub's `services:` ports syntax cannot restrict the bind interface, and the job's steps run directly on the runner (not in a container), so a published port is how they reach it at all. Safe on GitHub-hosted ephemeral runners; revisit if vars.HEAVY_RUNNER is ever pointed at a shared self-hosted runner — the fix is to run the job steps inside a container so service networking stays internal (which would conflict with the host-bound nextest archive).

Brutal-honesty charge 2/3 (accepted, NOT fixed — deliberately out of a CI phase's scope). Phase 4 fixed EMAILIBRIUM_DATABASE_URL, a flat TOP-LEVEL key. The same bug class still swallows every flat multi-word field INSIDE a nested struct, because neither env provider can address that shape: EMAILIBRIUM_STORE_QDRANT_URL splits to store.qdrant.url and flattens to store_qdrant_url, and serde ignores both. Confirmed silently dropped, all four advertised in docs/configuration-reference.md as the canonical examples of the env-override mechanism: EMAILIBRIUM_EMBEDDING_CACHE_SIZE (embedding.cache_size), EMAILIBRIUM_ENCRYPTION_MASTER_PASSWORD (encryption.master_password), EMAILIBRIUM_BACKUP_INTERVAL_SECS (backup.interval_secs), EMAILIBRIUM_LEARNING_SONA_ENABLED (learning.sona_enabled). The encryption one is the worst: configuration-reference.md:133 says 'Never set in config files; use env var or Docker secret', encryption.rs:97 reads only config.encryption.master_password, and the config field security.encryption_key_env that would imply a direct env read is consumed NOWHERE in backend/ — so an operator who follows the documented guidance gets 'Master password required' at startup. docker-compose.yml:46 sets one of these vars and it does nothing (now disclosed in-file). Pre-existing since the initial commit (95ad97a), not introduced by this pipeline. CANDIDATE FIX: a third figment provider splitting on the FIRST underscore only (store_qdrant_url -> store.qdrant_url), merged between the split and unsplit providers — it widens what resolves without changing any variable that resolves today. Needs its own review + a configuration-reference.md accuracy pass; likely an ADR amendment since it changes the env contract.

Brutal-honesty probe 5, completed by the defense: `gh api repos/pacphi/emailibrium/branches/develop/protection` returns 404 'Branch not protected', so rust-test-postgres (and every other check) is NOT a GitHub-required status check on the integration branch. The phase's claim 'CI actually proves PostgreSQL works' therefore holds for autopilot's own merges — its pr_ci playbook refuses to merge a red or check-less PR — but nothing mechanically stops a human from merging a PR whose PostgreSQL job failed or never ran. Fix is repo configuration, not code: enable branch protection on develop requiring at minimum 'Rust Tests (PostgreSQL)' and 'Compose Smoke Test'.
